subject: Customer request: masked log visibility and targeted erasure attestation
messages:
From: Laura Barnes <laura.barnes@medsafe.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: CISO Team <security@medsafe.io>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: sample of masked logs + attestation for targeted erasure

Hi Marissa,

Hope you are well. MedSafe is preparing for an external compliance review and our auditors asked for two items related to tenant-scoped logs:

1) A short sample showing the masked/logging posture you apply to tenant request logs (redacted where appropriate). We only need a small CSV sample (no PII) that illustrates fields, masks, and TTL.

2) A signed attestation describing the targeted erasure workflow for tenant-scoped logs (how we map a SAR/del request to deletion actions, scan tools used, and proof-of-delete artifacts if available).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide these and an estimate for turnaround? Our audit window is tight — ideally we need something by EOD Tue Nov 9 PT.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20m call if that helps.

Best,
Laura Barnes
Head of Compliance, MedSafe
(attachment: request-checklist.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Barnes <laura.barnes@medsafe.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sample of masked logs + attestation for targeted erasure

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide both items. Quick plan: 

- Karthik will produce a small, anonymized CSV that demonstrates mask patterns and TTL metadata.
- Soojin will draft an attestation tailored for the auditor language (SOC2-friendly).
- We will include an internal erasure-scan PDF showing the one-off proof-of-delete workflow and examples of the hashes we store for retention evidence.

Questions for you before we prepare:
1) Do you want the CSV to include any synthetic request IDs that map to your tenant IDs, or should those be fully synthetic?
2) For proof-of-delete, do your auditors prefer salted SHA256 hashes or a signed deletion certificate? We can provide either.

We should be able to turn this around within 48 hours if you confirm the preferences. If EOD Tue Nov 9 PT is strict, we can prioritize the minimal package and follow up with fuller docs.

Assigning Karthik and Soojin; looping them in.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: none)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Barnes <laura.barnes@medsafe.io>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sample of masked logs + attestation for targeted erasure

Hi all — quick technical response and attached samples.

Summary:
- Masking: We apply deterministic redaction for PII fields in request logs (email, phone) and store a hashed reference in a separate index. The sample CSV shows three rows with the following columns: timestamp, tenant_id_hash, request_type, masked_payload_preview, retention_ttl_days. No plaintext PII in sample.
- TTL: Tenant-scoped request logs default to 90 days; ephemeral session artifacts are 7 days unless a preserve flag is set for forensic holds. The sample includes a retention_ttl_days column.
- Erasure workflow: When a tenant requests deletion, our pipeline triggers an erasure job that: 1) queues items by tenant_hash, 2) runs a verification pass that compares pre-deletion hashes to the audit index, 3) writes a deletion record with a SHA256 hash of the removed object and timestamp. The attached erasure-scan-20271106.pdf is an internal export demonstrating the verification process and an example deletion record.

Attachment stubs: (attachment: masked-log-sample.csv — CSV, 10KB), (attachment: erasure-scan-20271106.pdf — PDF, 48KB)

Answers to Marissa's questions:
1) We will use fully synthetic tenant IDs in the CSV.
2) We can provide salted SHA256 hashes for proof-of-delete; if you need a signed certificate we can generate a DocuSign certificate as an added step (adds ~1 day).

Let us know if auditors need the exact salt format; otherwise we'll include the salt description in the attestation.

-Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Barnes <laura.barnes@medsafe.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 12:32:00 -0700
Subject: Draft attestation: targeted erasure and masked-log handling (for auditor)

Hi Laura — attaching a short attestation below; happy to revise language for your external auditor. This draft is written to be compatible with SOC2 control language and we will provide it as a signed PDF once you confirm.

--- Attestation (draft) ---
Redwood Inference attests that for tenant-scoped request logs:
1) No plaintext customer PII is stored in provided samples; all PII fields are masked and an irreversible salted hash is retained for correlation and audit.
2) Default retention for tenant-scoped request logs is 90 days, with ephemeral session artifacts retained for 7 days. Retention can be extended only under documented forensic hold procedures.
3) Targeted erasure requests (SARs) are processed by an automated erasure pipeline which identifies records by tenant_hash, executes removal from active indexes and cold storage, and performs a verification pass comparing pre-removal and post-removal hashes.
4) Proof-of-delete artifacts include salted SHA256 deletion hashes and a deletion record containing timestamp, operator (service account), and job id. When requested, Redwood can provide hashed proof-of-delete for specific tenant identifiers or a third-party notarized certificate.

This attestation is provided for audit purposes and is intended to describe our operational controls as of the date of issuance.

--- end attestation ---

If that reads OK, we'll package the attestation as a signed PDF and include the two attachments Karthik prepared. If you prefer DocuSign for the certificate, say the word and we'll initiate.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment: attestation-draft.txt)

From: Laura Barnes <laura.barnes@medsafe.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: CISO Team <security@medsafe.io>, Auditor <auditor@compliancehub.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sample of masked logs + attestation for targeted erasure

Marissa / team — thank you, this is exactly what we needed for the first tranche. The CSV sample and the attestation draft look good. Two small follow-ups from auditors:

1) Can you provide a salted SHA256 proof-of-delete for tenant_id_hash = "t-6f2a4c" in the sample set? The auditor wants to spot-check one deletion record versus the sample hash.
2) Please include the salt disclosure (not the salt value itself) and the signing mechanism for the deletion record in the final PDF.

If you can send 1) as a short text file and 2) as the finalized signed attestation by EOD Wed Nov 10 PT, we are set. We will confirm whether they need DocuSign for the certificate.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Laura
(attachment: auditor-followups.txt)
